entities.name: HDAC5-like protein
observations: The 751-residue query has 76% identity and 95.6% query coverage to reviewed vertebrate histone deacetylase 5 proteins, with E-value 0.
The sequence contains an N-terminal HDAC4_Gln Pfam domain at residues 75–163 and a large C-terminal region homologous to class IIa histone deacetylases.
Sequence-derived molecular weight is approximately 83.5 kDa and theoretical pI is approximately 7.40.
The protein is predicted to be soluble; the sequence has no evident long hydrophobic transmembrane segment or signal peptide.
The N-terminal region is rich in glutamine, lysine, acidic residues, serine, proline, and low-complexity segments, consistent with regulatory phosphorylation and protein-interaction regions.

entities.name: Histone deacetylase 5
observations: Reviewed vertebrate HDAC5 annotations describe lysine deacetylation of core histones H2A, H2B, H3, and H4, generally as part of multiprotein transcriptional repression complexes.
HDAC5 localizes to the nucleus and cytoplasm and can shuttle between them; muscle differentiation-associated export depends on phosphorylation and 14-3-3 binding.
Reported biological roles include repression of MEF2C-dependent transcription during muscle maturation, regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II, and corepression involving RARA.
Human HDAC5 is inhibited by trichostatin A and is associated with histone deacetylase complexes, nucleoplasm, nuclear speckles, and cytosol.

entities.name: HDAC4_Gln domain
observations: Pfam HDAC4_Gln domain PF12203.14 was detected in the query at residues 75–163 with i-Evalue 4.5e-32.
This domain supports membership in the class IIa HDAC regulatory protein family but is not itself sufficient to establish the complete catalytic mechanism.
